final_answer: The Dead Sea is called "dead" because its extremely high salinity prevents most aquatic life from surviving. This salinity results from geological and chemical processes. The sea lies in a rift valley, part of the Great Rift Valley system, where tectonic activity has shaped the region. Over millennia, mineral-rich water from surrounding areas flowed into the basin, but with no natural outlet, water evaporates, leaving behind dissolved salts. This process, combined with mineral deposits from surrounding rocks, has created one of the saltiest bodies of water on Earth. The high concentration of minerals like magnesium, potassium, and calcium further increases salinity, making it inhospitable to most organisms.
